# dsh-portable
**Offline and online export/import for DeepSeek Harness: pack a whole working DSH home into one `.ds
hpkg` file and restore it on another machine — no network, no `pnpm install`, no manual path fixing.
kg` file and restore it on another machine — no network, no `pnpm install`, no manual path fixing.**
中文说明 · CHANGELOG · PUBLISHING · HANDOFF
## Why
Moving a DSH setup between machines is painful for three reasons:
1. A working profile is not one file. It is `profiles/<name>/` plus plugins **with their `node_modul

es`**, skills, hooks, task boards, storages, `AGENTS.md`, installed runtimes, and session logs.
2. P
lugins are installed by pnpm from the network. An air-gapped machine, a locked-down corporate laptop

, or a machine behind a dead proxy simply cannot run `dsh plugin add`.
3. Configuration files embed
absolute paths (`C:\\Users\\me\\.dsh`, `/home/me/.dsh`) and the profile name, so copying the directo
ry tree produces a DSH that boots with broken plugin paths.
dsh-portable solves all three: it packages a whitelist of roots into a single self-describing archiv
e, refuses to walk outside that whitelist, and on import rewrites the six configuration files that a
ctually contain machine-local paths.
## What goes into a package
| Root | Path | Default |

| profile | `profiles/<name>` (config **and** plugin `node_modules`) | always |
| skills | `skills`

| always |
| skills-disabled | `skills-disabled` (skills the host disabled) | **opt-in, off by defau

lt** (`includeDisabledSkills`) |
| hooks | `hooks` | always |
| storages | `storages` | always |
| t

ask boards | task-board / todo-board storage | always |
| browser host | dsh-builtin-browser-host |

always |
| agent instructions | `AGENTS.md` | always |
| sessions | session logs | opt-in (`includeS

essions`) |
| runtimes | downloaded runtimes | opt-in (`includeRuntimes`) |
| credentials | `.creden

tials.yaml` | **opt-in, off by default** |
| source maps | `*.map` inside the package | on (`include

SourceMaps`) |
| backups | `*.bak-*` next to config files | off (`includeBackups`) |
> `skills-disabled` used to be included unconditionally (86% of a real package's size); it now behav
es like the other optional roots and rides along only when the checkbox is set or `includeDisabledSk
ills: true` is passed.
Anything not listed is never collected — there is no recursive "copy the whole home directory" step
anywhere in the code.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The plugin has to be registered in the profile's own `package.json` — under `dependencies` **and** `
dsh.profile.bundles`. Copying the package directory into `profiles/<profile>/node_modules` by hand l
ooks like it works, until that profile runs `npm install` again: npm treats an undeclared package as
extraneous and deletes it, and from then on the panel still renders its cards while every request a
nswers `404`. `dsh plugin add` (or `npm install dsh-portable` inside the profile) writes both halves
swers `404`. `dsh plugin add` (or `npm install dsh-portable` inside the profile) writes both halves.
Then open **DSH settings → Portable Migration** (便携迁移). The panel is registered at `settings.section
` with order 70, and is bilingual (zh/en) automatically.
Nothing is written to the DSH home until you press a button.
## Using the panel
Six cards:
1. **Export** — pick which optional roots to include, name the file, press Export. Packing runs in a
worker thread; the progress bar streams entry counts, and a 20 MB package over ~14 000 entries take
s about 3 seconds. An optional **passphrase** (leave empty to skip encryption) wraps the whole packa

ge in AES-256-GCM — a lost passphrase cannot be recovered.
2. **Packages** — every `.dshpkg` under `
<DSH_HOME>/dsh-portable/exports`, with size, modification time and buttons: Select / Download / Shar
e / Delete (delete asks for confirmation); encrypted packages carry an "encrypted" marker. *Select*
marks a package for the Import card below; *Download* pulls the file in chunks with an in-panel prog
ress bar and real resume support (bytes go straight to disk when the host offers the File System Acc
ess API; very large packages fall back to the browser's own downloader) — the LAN share is only reac

hable while both machines are on the same network.
3. **Upload** — drag or pick a `.dshpkg` and it i
s streamed to disk (`.part` then rename) with a live percentage, so a 2 GB package never sits in mem

ory; encrypted packages upload the same way.
4. **Import** — pick merge or replace (the active choic
e is highlighted), press *Preview* first (zero writes), then *Run import* — which opens an inline co
nfirmation before anything is written. **Sub-path selection**: after a preview you can check which t
op-level items to import and/or type package-relative extra paths (e.g. `skills/my-skill`); the two
combine as a union, and leaving both empty imports everything. Replace mode moves only the selected
paths aside. Encrypted packages ask for their passphrase first. The result is a small key/value summ
ary: applied items, rewritten paths, backup folder, included paths and warnings, plus the plugin-lis
t merge (bundles kept from this machine, bundles the package needs but this machine lacks). Restart

DSH after the import for the written configuration to take effect.
[该节后续省略]
## Compatibility

- DSH `>= 0.1.7-rc.2`
- Node `^22.15.0 || >= 24.0.0`
- Windows, macOS, Linux (long paths handled thr
ough the `\\?\` prefix on Windows)
## Limitations

- Session logs are opt-in because they contain conversation content.
- Encryption is optional and th
ere is no signature: a package exported without a passphrase is a plain tar — encrypt it or use encr

ypted media when it carries credentials. A lost passphrase cannot be recovered.
- The sub-path selec

tor matches **logical path prefixes** (directory or file level); there is no glob support.
- Symlink
s that point outside the DSH home are packaged as links but will fail to be recreated on Windows wit
hout developer mode; that failure is a warning, not an abort.
